sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale

announcements.name: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (production ready)
announcements.shortDescription: Now includes a built-in harness integrated with skills, memory, and middleware, plus plug-in integrations for the GitHub Copilot SDK and Claude Agent SDK [inferred]
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft Agent Framework is now at version 1.0 and production ready. As Jeff demonstrated, it now has a built-in harness that is well integrated with skills, memory, and middleware. It also includes plug-in integrations with harnesses such as the GitHub Copilot SDK and the Claude Agent SDK [inferred].

announcements.name: Foundry Toolkit for VS Code (generally available)
announcements.shortDescription: A purpose-built developer experience for building Foundry agents without leaving the editor
announcements.longDescription: Foundry Toolkit for VS Code is now generally available. It provides a purpose-built developer experience for building Foundry agents without the developer ever having to leave the editor.

announcements.name: Foundry Toolbox (generally available soon)
announcements.shortDescription: A single managed, MCP-compatible endpoint for all agent tools with governance, guardrails, and a tool-search feature to optimize context usage
announcements.longDescription: Tool boxes in Foundry are becoming generally available soon. They provide one single managed endpoint for all the tools that make agents powerful, with the right governance and policy in place. Skills are now a first-class integration with tool boxes as well.

announcements.name: Voice Live integration with Foundry Agent Service
announcements.shortDescription: GA for prompt agents and public preview for hosted agents
announcements.longDescription: Voice Live integration with Foundry Agent Service is generally available today for prompt agents and in public preview for hosted agents. It supports speech and voice scenarios for agents.

announcements.name: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service (generally available soon)
announcements.shortDescription: Per-session sandbox isolation, sub-second cold start, zero idle-time cost, framework-agnostic, supporting long-running autonomous agents with durable state and file-system access
announcements.longDescription: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service are becoming generally available soon, offering per-session sandbox isolation, sub-second cold start, zero idle-time cost, and a framework-agnostic design. Foundry hosted agents now even support long-running autonomous agents such as Open Claw [inferred] and Hermes agents, all with durable state execution and file-system access.

announcements.name: Routines (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Event-driven triggers that turn reactive agents into proactive, long-running ones via queued, tracked runs
announcements.longDescription: Routines in Foundry Agent Service are now in public preview. Routines are what make an agent go from reactive to proactive and make it long-running: the developer decides what needs to happen, and Foundry then queues, executes, and tracks every single run. This is how you turn a reactive one-off task into a proactive, continuous agent.

announcements.name: Publish to Microsoft 365 Teams and Copilot (GA soon); Autopilot agents (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Agents inherit identity, policy, and permissions, and Autopilot agents gain their own IDs, email addresses, and Teams presence, governed in Agent 365
announcements.longDescription: Publishing to Microsoft 365 Teams and Copilot is generally available soon, allowing developers to publish all their Foundry agents directly into Teams and Copilot where teams already work, with identity, policy, and permissions flowing through automatically. In addition, developers can now publish Foundry agents as Autopilot agents into Teams, now in public preview. These Autopilot agents can take on their own IDs, email addresses, and even Teams presence so they can initiate conversations or follow up on action items, all governed end to end in Agent 365.

announcements.name: Rubric for custom evaluation (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Auto-generates context-aware, weighted scoring criteria for evaluation and optimization
announcements.longDescription: Rubric for custom evaluation is now in public preview. Rubric auto-generates context-aware criteria and weighted scoring to define what good looks like for both evaluation and optimization, so the developer doesn't have to start from scratch.

announcements.name: Agent Optimizer for Foundry Agent Service (private preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Turns production traces and evals into ranked candidate agents by tweaking skills, prompts, tool configuration, and models, compared across quality, cost, and latency
announcements.longDescription: Agent Optimizer for Foundry Agent Service is now in private preview. It turns production traces and evals into a set of ranked candidates by tweaking skills, prompts, tool configuration, and even models. These ranked candidates are shown side by side across quality, cost, and latency, and the developer remains in control to choose the exact winning variant to promote, with trace-back, lineage, and rollback available when needed.

announcements.name: Procedural memory (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Lets agents learn a playbook across sessions rather than relearning each conversation
announcements.longDescription: Procedural memory in Foundry Agent Service is now in public preview. It empowers the agent to learn the playbook across all sessions, so the agent doesn't have to start learning from scratch in every conversation. There is no manual rewrite of prompts or skills; the agent becomes smarter, safer, and cheaper the more it runs, all with the developer in control for every change.
